title: io.ReadAll on request body in binding middleware — no MaxBytesReader
rationale: Replaced io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBindingBodyBytes+1) with http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBindingBodyBytes). MaxBytesReader caps allocation AND closes the connection on overrun, preventing slow-drip goroutine exhaustion. Detects *http.MaxBytesError via errors.As; removed now-redundant post-read len check. Tightened limit from 1MiB to 64KiB.
variants_checked: binding.go:checkRequestBinding — patched; mcp.go, a2a.go — no direct body reads; revocation/status.go, anchor/rfc3161.go, resolver/did.go — outbound client reads, already bounded separately
bypass_considered: Slow-drip attack with Content-Length:100 but 100MB actual body: MaxBytesReader fires at 64KiB+1, connection marked for close, goroutine exits promptly
test_note: TestCheckRequestBindingLenientOversizedBodyReturns413 added to binding_test.go covering lenient-mode path previously untested
review_reason: The diff is scoped entirely to binding.go and its test file, replacing the broken io.LimitReader+post-read-length-check pattern with http.MaxBytesReader — the same pattern already established at cmd/server/main.go:321. The errors.As branch correctly distinguishes oversize from other read errors without trusting any attacker-supplied data, and the 1MiB→64KiB constant reduction is a tightening, not a weakening.
